Your employer: contracts, credits, staff, evidence and what the corporation wants.

The company

The company is not a faction you befriend. It is an account, a queue of requests, and a bill.

Nothing the company asks for has a deadline

There are no deadlines in this mod. No request, contract, offer, quote or trade ever expires. There is no penalty for taking a long time, no cancellation for slowness, and nothing that asks you to respond within a set period.

You may cancel a job. The corporation may not.

The only thing in this mod with a duration is a gate's open connection, and that duration is a consequence of power, technology, maintenance and staffing — all things you control. See Gates and connections.

Every job has more than one way to finish

Every request and contract offers at least two routes to success, of at least two different kinds. The kinds are:

RouteWhat it means
DeliverBring the thing back
DocumentBring the record back instead of the thing
SubstituteSatisfy it with a different item of the same capability
PurchaseBuy the shortfall through procurement
TestifyA staff member's account, where a crew saw what a record would show
Decline and redirectRefuse the stated task and complete a related one
ResearchComplete a named company project

The corporation does not care how a branch succeeds.

Two kinds of money

The accountA ledger in dollars. Pays staff, site fees, procurement, obligations. Never spawned as silver.
Physical stockSilver, steel, food, gear, salvage. Ordinary RimWorld goods, behaving exactly as always.

The Ledger pane lists recent movements with a reason for each. Unpaid obligations do not quietly vanish — pay them from Overview.

Bonds

The account can be printed as bearer bonds, in denominations from ten up to a quadrillion.

Named for their valueA bond says what it is worth
DepositPut one back in, from the paper itself, at full value
CombineFold several into the fewest
A beaconBanks every bond in a radius at once, also at full value

A bond is not sold. It is already credits, so banking it is what happens to it — the company declines to buy one, because selling a bond at a discount would lose you money by accident.

Ordinary valuables are a separate trade. Sell those to the company and you receive 85% of their worth: instant, with no trader, caravan or travel, and the company takes a cut for that.

Paper raises colony wealth where the ledger does not. Liquidity costs risk, and paper burns.

Requests and contracts

RequestWhat the corporation asks for next. Finish one and the next opens.
ContractA priced job with terms, a base payment and a bonus.

The opening is a tutorial that becomes a campaign. Six requests teach the systems in dependency order — power the gate, assemble and calibrate it, bring back one record, mark a route home, report a disagreement, hold a connection open.

The seventh is the hinge: the corporation asks you to choose a direction. You may declare one, or go and do the work in one without announcing anything. Every choice succeeds.

After the hinge the corporation keeps asking, and stops teaching. Later requests are generated from your branch's state, your coordinate history and what you can do.

The Contracts pane shows both, requests first.

The arcs

The campaign is laid out in eight arcs. Each adds a kind of work rather than a difficulty step.

1. Keep the doors openPower the site, assign an operator, bring home a record
2. Measure before trustingFamiliar spaces reveal patterns; reports disagree
3. Return with controlKnown destinations become working routes
4. Make a business of itClients request surveys, samples, instruments, rescue, access
5. Build beyond headquartersRemote sites need people, supplies, signals, protection, an exit
6. Respond to the outside worldOpenings appear in towns; witnesses and missing residents
7. Expand industrial reachHeavy cargo and staff across the wider world
8. Enter deeper systemsKnown families combine, then one unfamiliar rule at a time

Staff

Hire, pay, and assign company roles. Pawn autonomy and ordinary RimWorld skills and traits are untouched.

Certification

Some jobs need a certificate, and you train people into them. A gate operator, a field analyst and a reserve technician each have a train bill:

CertificateNeeds
Gate operatorIntellectual 4
Field analystIntellectual 3
Reserve technicianCrafting 5

The first two run on a machining table or a crafting spot; the third needs the table. Training is work over time, and it completes by making that person certified.

A branch with no certified gate operator cannot open a connection. The remedy is a bill, not a recruitment drive.

Field history and reporting in

Field history is kept per person. The crew planner shows who is a novice, who is a veteran, and who has walked the address you are dialling.

Anybody back from a crossing is not dispatched again until debriefed. Quarantine and debrief are one thing: you do not go back out until you have reported in.

Walking a single colonist through a door by hand is not a company dispatch and is not held to it.

Research

Insight from analysed records buys unlocks across nine branches:

Branch
Gate engineering and stabilityThe window ladder, telemetry, standing connections
Facilities and powerReserve capacity, protected rooms, repair practice
Fieldcraft and medicineKits, triage, recovery, training, rescue teams
Measurement and evidenceSensors, comparison, confidence, client reports
Spatial mapping and topologyAtlases, alternate exits, deeper surveys
Entities and containmentDetection, quarantine, scoped study
Communications and logisticsLink range, delivery planning, caches, relays
Commerce and organisationBetter offers, specialist recruitment, leases
Transport and orbital supportExpansion content only, and never required

Branches run through five progression bands:

BandWhat it is for
0 — Facility foundationsMake the company safe enough to work
1 — First entryPrepare a measured short expedition and read a first return
2 — Repeatable operationsRevisit known coordinates; reduce preventable failures
3 — Remote operationsSupport more than one site; work beyond headquarters
4 — Deep operationsCombine known techniques; extend reach

A band is a progression band, not a single chain. Every band above the first is reachable by more than one path, so a branch is never locked behind one project you have not happened to unlock.

A project's prerequisites are only ever completed logs, a named project below it, and the insight price. Nothing requires time to have passed.

Every unlock grants a capability that real behaviour honours.

Facilities, equipment and sites

FacilityA contiguous run of space the branch treats as one place
Equipment linkWires a shelf, analyser or cabinet into a gate — across distance and through walls, made by hand
SiteSomewhere beyond headquarters, on the books. Billed daily, needs people present to receive anything, stops being billed while out of reach

Nothing about a link is automatic.

Work across a connection

Colonists travel through an open connection to do work on the other side: hauling, construction, bills, research, medical, cooking, cleaning, mining, hunting, farming, animals.

  • Work you started keeps going. A pawn who crossed to finish a job finishes it.
  • Work you have not started waits. A far-side job sits below every local job of the same type, so nobody walks through a gate while the same work exists at home.

The Activity and Connected Work panes report what crossed, and why.

Places held open, and giving one back

Every place you hold open costs a loaded map, as a colony does. The Places pane shows the count against your allowance and lets you hand one back.

Releasing a place is permanent, and the confirmation says so: the gate will not open again.

Before you release
Anything left there is lostThe pane counts the items and tells you how many
Not with people insideRefused while anybody is there, or part-way through crossing
Not your headquartersRefused outright

A place you found rather than built is a gentler case. Releasing one moves it to a second list, and selecting the door that led there offers it back.

When a crew does not come home

A return window can expire with people still on the far side. They are not dead and they are not removed.

The crew and their cargo stay at the saved address. There are two ways to recover them:

  1. Restore the gate and reopen that route. Fix whatever failed — power, calibration, the operator — and dial the same address.
  2. Send a relief trip. One extra person per run, and the same relief member is reused for further attempts. The original crew is unchanged.

A closed gate does not take your people with it.

Containment

Holding platforms and what they can hold are the base game's.

What this adds is warnings about the maps you are not looking at — RimWorld's own containment alerts read the map on screen, and here several maps are live at once.

On a breach the branch cuts every open connection. Armed by default, using each gate's own emergency cutoff.

A branch never dies

Once a branch is in contact with the corporation, it is not written off.

If everyone at the laboratory goes down — not dead, down — the company arrives.

The site is cleared, and nobody who was there is left standing
The dead are buried on the property, or burned where no ground will take a grave
Damage is repaired, every connection is shut at the gate
Three replacement staff land with supplies
Every bond anywhere on your maps is taken
Up to 25,000,000 is drawn from the account — whatever is there, never below zero

You never lose the game. The gate is left commissioned, so the new crew can bring it back up.

The letter gives you the figures. There is no limit on how many times this happens and no escalating penalty: an investor protecting an investment does not withdraw it for slowness.

The other two openings keep a gentler version, and only once the branch has earned contact: a clean-up team that arrives after everyone is actually dead, and leaves five.

Rimrooms — Async Industries. A development build; nothing here is a balance, performance or compatibility report.
